confidence_notes: Restaurant and coffee anchors rest on several 2025-2026 aggregated sources (combien-coute cappuccino and lunch/dinner averages, Athens and Greece Numbeo-based figures, one Mykonos expat guide) and are reasonably supported. Beer, cocktail and wine are weaker: the only Mykonos beer figure is a EUR 5 draft price, and no direct wine price was found, so wine_glass is inferred from beer using a typical Greek resort ratio of about 1.5x and cocktail from about 2.5x beer, with the cocktail figure also checked against a EUR 6-8 budget-bar report. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July high season from general knowledge, not from live listings or booking pages. The EUR-to-USD conversion used for the USD anchors (about 1.16) is an assumption from general knowledge and was not searched. The FX observation is the most recent official RBA figure I could verify (20 March 2026), not the latest available on 16 October 2026; I could not retrieve the RBA F11.1 table for later dates. Overall, treat the figures as bounded planning estimates with roughly +/-25% uncertainty, and more for accommodation and drinks.
comparable_city_reasoning: Restaurant and coffee prices are based on Greek national and Athens figures (Numbeo-based) with a Mykonos tourist premium of roughly 1.5 to 2x for mid-range dining, following the Mykonos-specific estimates. Drinks are based on the local Mykonos beer price, with cocktail and wine set by ratio to beer. Accommodation is a holistic estimate for mid-to-high-season Cycladic island pricing, comparable to other Greek island resort towns in July.
